about: 3 temperament traits and one line of text per entry, keyed by Dogs Australia name (official breeds) or bonus name. Traits come from the fixed list of 16. source: 'standard' = derived from the Dogs Australia standard's Temperament/Characteristics wording (the standard text itself is not stored); 'research' = gaps filled from other standard sections, Wikipedia and breed guides. text: our own words, never copied from a standard.

Affenpinscher.text: A monkey-faced little dog with a serious air about it. Fond of its family and fiercely loyal.

Afghan Hound.text: Elegant and aloof, seeming to look right through you. Thinks for itself and is not quick to obey.

Airedale Terrier.text: The largest of the terriers. Friendly and confident, with a proud bearing and real courage.

Akita.text: A powerful Japanese dog with a curled tail and a quiet, noble manner. Loyal to family but aloof with strangers and other dogs.

Akita (Japanese).text: A powerful, composed Japanese breed that's deeply devoted to its family. Carries itself with quiet dignity.

Alaskan Malamute.text: A big, strong Arctic sled dog with a friendly, outgoing nature. Loves its people, though it can be a handful to train.

American Bully.text: A muscly, compact bully breed that's usually a big softie at home. Confident and loves games like tug.

American Hairless Terrier.text: A lively, smart terrier that's mostly bald. Keen-eyed, playful and always ready for action.

American Staffordshire Terrier.text: Confident and strong, but usually a softie with its people. Famous for courage and devotion.

Anatolian Shepherd Dog.text: A large Turkish flock guardian, steady and self-assured. Quietly watchful and built for long days on the job.

Australasian Bosdog.text: An Aussie-developed bulldog breed, stocky and strong. Loyal and affectionate, and friendly with people of all ages.

Australian Cattle Dog.text: Smart, tough and protective of its people. Bred to work all day, so it needs a job and lots of exercise.

Australian Kelpie.text: The classic Aussie sheepdog with endless drive. Loyal, sharp-eyed and happiest with work to do.

Australian Shepherd.text: A brainy, tireless herder, often with striking merle coats and eyes. Needs plenty to keep it busy.

Australian Silky Terrier.text: A true terrier in a silky coat - keen, busy and quick to bark. Loving at home but has a stubborn streak.

Australian Stumpy Tail Cattle Dog.text: A lean Aussie cattle dog born with a stumpy tail. Watchful and quick to learn, devoted to family.

Australian Terrier.text: A tough little Aussie worker bred to deal with snakes and rats. Devoted and loving with its family.

Azawakh.text: A tall, ultra-lean sighthound from the Sahel. Gentle with family, aloof with strangers and very watchful.

Basenji.text: The barkless dog, known to yodel instead. Clever and cat-like, with a strong mind of its own.

Basset Fauve De Bretagne.text: A small, wiry, fawn hound from Brittany. Cheerful, loving and tireless on a scent trail.

Basset Hound.text: Long ears, short legs and a nose that never quits. Laid-back and loving, with a famously stubborn streak.

Bavarian Mountain Scent Hound.text: A German tracking specialist. Calm and devoted to its owner, though reserved with strangers.

Beagle.text: A sociable pack hound led by its nose. Food-mad and vocal, with a famous baying howl.

Bearded Collie.text: A shaggy, bouncy herder with a happy-go-lucky streak. Bright and full of beans outdoors, then settles nicely at home.

Beauceron (Berger de Beauce).text: A big, fearless French herder that's gentle with its family. Naturally wary of strangers and makes a serious guard dog.

Bedlington Terrier.text: Looks like a little lamb but has a terrier's pluck. Sweet with its people and happy to say hello.

Belgian Shepherd Dog (Groenendael, Tervu.text: Sharp, watchful and always ready to work. Fiercely devoted to its family and needs plenty of exercise and a job to do.

Bergamasco Shepherd Dog.text: A patient Italian sheepdog in a coat of felted flocks. Bonds closely with its people and keeps a watchful eye on them.

Berger Picard.text: A scruffy French sheepdog with big upright ears. Even-tempered and quick to learn, with a brave, steady nature.

Bernese Mountain Dog.text: A gentle giant that's devoted to its family. Easygoing at home and loves cool weather.

Bichon Frise.text: Cheerful, bouncy and keen to meet everyone. A white powder puff that loves a game and a cuddle.

Biewer Terrier.text: Small, silky and full of fun. Sticks close to its people and loves a game followed by a cuddle.

Black and Tan Coonhound.text: A big American scent hound with a booming bay. Easygoing with people, but focused on the trail.

Bloodhound.text: A gentle, soulful tracker with an unbeatable nose. Kind with people but will follow a scent anywhere.

Bluetick Coonhound.text: An athletic, loud-voiced scent hound built for the trail. Friendly at home but its nose leads the way.

Bolognese.text: A quiet, laid-back little cloud of a dog. Sticks close to its family and loves a cuddle.

Border Collie.text: Often called the smartest breed. Needs daily work, play or training to stay happy.

Border Terrier.text: A scruffy, otter-headed worker that's game for anything. Plenty of energy and grit for its size.

Borzoi.text: A tall, elegant Russian sighthound bred to course wolves. Quiet and aloof, but quick off the mark.

Boston Terrier.text: Dapper in its tuxedo markings. A bright, friendly little dog with plenty of bounce and a playful sense of fun.

Bouvier Des Flandres.text: A big, bearded Belgian farm dog built for herding and hauling. Smart and steady, happiest with a job to do.

Boxer.text: Bouncy and fun-loving, a great family dog. Stays puppyish for years and loves a romp.

Bracco Italiano.text: An old Italian pointing dog with droopy ears and a gentle face. Calm at home and keen to work.

Briard.text: A bold, shaggy French herder with a long beard. Clever, lively and loyal, with a strong instinct to watch over its family.

British Bulldog.text: Stocky and determined-looking, but usually a kind, easy-going couch companion. Loyal and courageous at heart.

Brittany.text: A lively, compact bird dog with heaps of stamina. Friendly, game and happiest with a job to do.

Bull Arab.text: An Australian pig-hunting dog that's placid and kind at home. Very driven when working and can be strong-willed.

Bull Terrier.text: A comic, strong-willed dog that loves people. Needs firm, fun training and lots of exercise.

Bull Terrier (Miniature).text: A fun-loving clown with a big personality in a compact body. Plucky and a bit stubborn.

Bullmastiff.text: Bred to help gamekeepers catch poachers. Big and loyal, it stays alert but usually prefers a short walk and a long nap.

Cairn Terrier.text: A scrappy, cheerful little worker that's always up for adventure. Confident with a mind of its own.

Canaan Dog.text: An ancient desert dog from the Middle East. Alert and quick to sound the alarm, loyal to family and friendly once settled.

Canadian Eskimo Dog.text: A rugged Arctic sled dog bred to haul in harsh conditions. Hard-working, but gentle and affectionate with its people.

Cane Corso.text: A muscular Italian guardian that needs firm, consistent training and an active life. Loves to have a job to do.

Caucasian Shepherd Dog.text: A massive, thick-coated livestock guardian. Calm and dignified most of the time, but quick to act if it senses a threat.

Cavachon.text: A soft, fluffy Cavalier-Bichon mix made for companionship. Sweet-natured and up for a gentle game.

Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.text: Friendly with everyone, dogs included. Happy on the couch or on a walk.

Cavoodle.text: A small, curly companion mixing Cavalier sweetness with Poodle brains. Loves people and usually gets on with everyone.

Central Asian Shepherd Dog.text: An ancient, giant flock guardian with a calm, self-assured nature. Independent and thinks for itself, so not for beginners.

Cesky Terrier.text: A laid-back terrier from Czechia with a long, low build. Easygoing, friendly and keen to please.

Chesapeake Bay Retriever.text: A tough duck dog with an oily, wavy coat built for icy water. Devoted, protective and bolder than most retrievers.

Chihuahua (Long Coat).text: Tiny but full of spirit and quick to sound the alarm. Often bonds tightly with one favourite person.

Chihuahua (Smooth Coat).text: Tiny but confident, often bonding closely with one person. Quick to bark at strangers.

Chinese Crested Dog.text: A cheerful, gentle-natured companion that loves being close to its people. Happy to play, then snuggle.

Chow Chow.text: A lion-like dog with a blue-black tongue. Proud and loyal to its family, but aloof and reserved with strangers.

Cirneco Dell'Etna.text: A sleek Sicilian hunting hound with big upright ears. Loving at home but thinks for itself.

Clumber Spaniel.text: A heavy, gentle spaniel that likes to take its time. Calm, friendly and quietly dignified.

Cocker Spaniel.text: A happy, tail-wagging gundog that loves to sniff and explore. Gentle and keen to please.

Cocker Spaniel (American).text: A merry, sweet-natured little spaniel. Loves people and makes an easy family companion.

Collie (Rough).text: The long-coated Lassie dog: graceful and devoted to its family. Bred for sheep work, so it still enjoys a job.

Collie (Smooth).text: A short-coated collie that's cheerful and sociable. Smart and quick to learn, with a herding dog's love of work.

Coton De Tulear.text: Sociable and easygoing with people and other dogs alike. Has a clownish, playful side.

Curly Coated Retriever.text: Covered in tight curls and built for water work. Confident and independent, with a proud bearing.

Dachshund - Standard Long, Standard Smoo.text: Brave and curious, with a big bark for its size. Loves to burrow, sniff and be with its people.

Dachshund Rabbit Long, Dachshund Rabbit.text: The tiniest dachshund, but still a determined little hunter. Friendly and even-tempered, with plenty of pluck.

Dalmatian.text: The spotty carriage dog, built for endurance and needing plenty of exercise. Outgoing and sociable with a proud bearing.

Dandie Dinmont Terrier.text: Long and low, with a fluffy topknot. Thinks for itself but is a loving, clever companion.

Deerhound.text: A huge, shaggy sighthound with a gentle soul. Calm and friendly, happy to lounge after a run.

Dobermann.text: Sleek, athletic and sharp as a tack. Fearless and watchful, yet often a real softie with its own family.

Dogue de Bordeaux.text: A huge-headed French mastiff with a big heart. Calm and loving at home, and naturally protective of its family.

Dutch Shepherd Dog.text: A brindle all-rounder that loves to work. Alert, eager and deeply loyal, it needs lots of exercise and mental challenge.

English Setter.text: A speckled, sweet-natured bird dog. Friendly and full of energy, it loves a good long run.

English Springer Spaniel.text: Bred to flush game and loves to be busy. Friendly and eager to learn, it's never far from the action.

English Toy Terrier (Black & Tan).text: A small terrier with old ratting instincts. Keen-eyed, lively and bolder than its size suggests.

Estrela Mountain Dog.text: A large Portuguese guardian from the Estrela mountains. Loving and loyal with family, but protective of its territory.

Eurasier.text: A fluffy, even-tempered spitz-type companion. Calm and watchful, close with family but reserved with strangers.

Field Spaniel.text: Mellow at home but lively in the field. A thoughtful spaniel that likes to do things its own way.

Finnish Lapphund.text: A fluffy reindeer herder from Lapland. Gentle and calm at home, but clever and brave when there's work to be done.

Finnish Spitz.text: A fox-red bird dog that barks to mark its quarry. Bold, energetic and fond of doing its own thing.

Flat Coated Retriever.text: An optimistic, tail-wagging retriever that never really grows up. Loves everyone and has energy to burn.

Fox Terrier (Smooth).text: Bred to bolt foxes and still keen as mustard. Sociable and bold, missing very little around it.

Fox Terrier (Wire).text: Wiry-coated and full of beans. Friendly and plucky, with ears pricked for anything happening nearby.

Foxhound.text: A good-natured pack hound with huge stamina. Mild-mannered and easy with people and other dogs.

French Bulldog.text: A cheerful companion that's happy in an apartment. Needs only short walks and dislikes the heat.

German Hunting Terrier.text: An intense, fearless little hunting dog that lives to work. Needs lots to do and firm, consistent training.

German Pinscher.text: A sleek, medium-sized ratter with plenty of zip. Watchful and lively, and friendly once it knows you.

German Shepherd Dog.text: Steady, protective and very trainable. Bonds closely with its family and is wary of strangers.

German Shepherd Dog (Long Stock Coat).text: A fluffier German Shepherd with the same steady, self-assured nature. Easy to train and keen to watch over its family.

German Shorthaired Pointer.text: A versatile gundog with tonnes of stamina. Friendly and keen to work, it needs plenty of exercise every day.

German Spitz (Mittel & Klein).text: A fluffy, fox-faced spitz with a curled tail. Bright, friendly and lively, it loves being part of the action.

German Wirehaired Pointer.text: A tough, versatile hunting dog with energy to spare. Bonds closely with its family and can be wary of strangers.

Glen Of Imaal Terrier.text: A sturdy Irish terrier that's quieter than most. Gentle at home but gutsy and active outdoors.

Golden Retriever.text: Patient and friendly, great with children. Thrives on company and a daily retrieve.

Gordon Setter.text: A striking black and tan setter from Scotland. Bright, friendly and bold, with loads of stamina.

Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen.text: A rough-coated French scent hound with a lot of drive. Brave and tireless, with its own agenda.

Great Dane.text: A towering dog with a gentle, friendly nature. Watchful at the door, but carries itself with real elegance.

Great Swiss Mountain Dog.text: A big tricolour Swiss farm dog bred to pull carts and guard. Confident and watchful, with a stately presence.

Greyhound.text: A gentle couch potato that loves a quick sprint. Affectionate, quiet and happy to snooze the day away.

Griffon Bruxellois.text: Bearded, bright-eyed and busy, with an almost human expression. Clever, lively and watchful.

Groodle.text: A big, bouncy family dog mixing Golden Retriever warmth with Poodle smarts. Sociable and keen to play.

Hamiltonstovare.text: A handsome Swedish hound with a keen nose. Even-tempered and sociable, but loves to follow a scent.

Harrier.text: Cheerful, sweet-natured pack hound that's great with people. Loves exploring and sniffing on long walks.

Havanese.text: Sociable and happy-go-lucky, with a soft, silky coat. Quick to learn tricks and loves to play.

Hungarian Vizsla.text: Known as a velcro dog: it sticks close to its people. Needs lots of running every day.

Hungarian Wirehaired Vizsla.text: A bearded, rust-coloured hunting dog. Clever and dignified, but a real softie with its family.

Ibizan Hound.text: A leggy, big-eared hunter with a famous springy leap. Lively outdoors, elegant and aloof indoors.

Icelandic Sheepdog.text: A cheerful spitz with a curly tail and a warm welcome for everyone. Keen, busy and happiest when it's on the move.

Irish Red and White Setter.text: Sweet-natured and affectionate, with a patchy red and white coat. Friendly and keen to please.

Irish Setter.text: A glamorous redhead with boundless energy. Outgoing, loving and fun to be around.

Irish Terrier.text: Bold and spirited with a reckless streak. Deeply devoted to its people, less patient with other dogs.

Irish Water Spaniel.text: Curly-coated, with a distinctive rat-like tail. A playful clown with its family but wary of new faces.

Irish Wolfhound.text: A towering giant with a soft heart. Quiet and gentle at home, despite its hunting heritage.

Italian Greyhound.text: A slim, affectionate sighthound that loves warmth and a sprint. Can be shy with strangers.

Italian Spinone.text: A shaggy, bearded hunting dog with a soft heart. Gentle, loyal and smarter than it looks.

Jack Russell Terrier.text: Small, tireless and always busy. Loves chasing and digging, and needs plenty to do.

Japanese Chin.text: Gentle and sweet-tempered, with a cat-like streak. Bright, friendly and happiest near its people.

Japanese Spitz.text: A fluffy white companion with a big smile. Loving with family, bright and quick to let you know someone's coming.

Jug.text: A Jack Russell-Pug cross that's feisty and fun. Loves cuddles but has terrier energy to burn.

Kangal Shepherd Dog.text: A powerful Turkish guardian with a black mask, bred to protect sheep from wolves. Calm and composed, but fearless.

Karelian Bear Dog.text: A bold black-and-white Finnish hunting dog, bred to face down bears. Brave, tireless and self-assured.

Keeshond.text: A fluffy Dutch barge dog with spectacle-like markings. Friendly and loving with family, and quick to sound the alarm.

Kerry Blue Terrier.text: A strong, smart terrier with a determined attitude. Playful with family but keeps a watchful eye out.

King Charles Spaniel.text: Soft-natured and devoted at home, though a bit shy with new people. A quiet, loving lap dog.

Komondor.text: Instantly recognisable by its long white cords. Bred to guard flocks alone, so it's brave, protective and wary of strangers.

Koolie.text: An Australian working sheepdog, often merle. Eager to please and devoted to its handler, needing plenty to do.

Kuvasz.text: A large white Hungarian guardian with a noble bearing. Devoted to its own people and fearless when it senses a threat.

Labradoodle.text: Bred in Australia as a guide dog cross. Sociable, quick to learn and usually gentle with kids.

Labrador Retriever.text: Gentle, food-motivated and keen to please. Loves water, fetch and nearly everyone it meets.

Lagotto Romagnolo.text: A curly Italian dog famous for sniffing out truffles. Loving, trainable and happiest when working.

Lakeland Terrier.text: Self-assured and spirited, with a proud little swagger. Friendly with people and brave to a fault.

Landseer (European Continental Type).text: A tall black-and-white cousin of the Newfoundland. Sweet-natured and patient, and usually a strong swimmer.

Large Munsterlander.text: A black and white German hunting dog. Devoted to its people and happiest with a job to do.

Leonberger.text: A gentle giant with a lion-like mane. Friendly with everyone and playful, yet carries itself with quiet dignity.

Lhasa Apso.text: A small Tibetan watchdog with a long coat. A clown with family, but self-assured and wary of strangers.

Lowchen (Little Lion Dog).text: Often clipped like a tiny lion. Bright, friendly and loving, it thrives on company and attention.

Maltese.text: Sweet natured and bright, thriving on company. Stays playful well into old age.

Maltese x Shih Tzu.text: A small, soft-coated lap dog that sticks close to its people. Usually easy-going, with short bursts of play.

Manchester Terrier.text: Sleek and black and tan, once a champion ratter. Watchful and devoted, but cool with strangers.

Maremma Sheepdog.text: A big white Italian flock guardian, used on Aussie farms to protect livestock. Calm, dignified and fiercely protective.

Mastiff.text: One of the heaviest breeds around. Calm and gentle, very affectionate with family and happy to lean on your legs.

Miniature American Shepherd.text: Like a pocket-sized Aussie Shepherd. Quick to learn, keen to work and closely bonded to its family.

Miniature Fox Terrier.text: A small, speedy Aussie ratter with a short, smooth coat. Bright and devoted, but will chase anything small.

Miniature Pinscher.text: Small but fearless, strutting about like it owns the place. Lively, alert and always on the go.

Mudi.text: A rare, wavy-coated Hungarian herder. Watchful, full of energy and bold, it thrives on activity and dog sports.

Murray River Retriever.text: A curly, liver-coloured Aussie duck dog from the Murray. Bright, loyal and full of energy for a swim or a run.

Neapolitan Mastiff.text: Famous for its loose, heavy wrinkles and jowls. Calm and devoted at home, and a serious guardian of its family.

Newfoundland.text: A huge, soft-hearted water dog with lifesaving roots. Famously patient with kids and devoted to its people.

Norfolk Terrier.text: Small but fearless, with a sunny, lovable nature. Gets along well and rarely picks fights.

Norwegian Buhund.text: A sturdy Nordic farm dog with a curled tail. Lively, cheerful and watchful, and quick to bark at anything new.

Norwegian Elkhound.text: A sturdy grey spitz bred to hunt moose. Friendly and smart, but likes to make its own decisions.

Norwich Terrier.text: A tough little terrier that's always on the go. Happy, lovable and not one to start trouble.

Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever.text: The smallest retriever, bred to lure ducks with playful antics. Smart, keen and full of energy.

Old English Sheepdog.text: A shaggy, amiable big dog with a goofy streak. Easy-going at home but loves a romp, with a booming bark.

Otterhound.text: A big, shaggy, amiable hound that loves water. Easygoing and clownish, with a booming voice.

Papillon.text: Named for its butterfly ears. Sharp as a tack, lively and quick to learn, it shines at tricks and agility.

Parson Russell Terrier.text: A busy, bold hunting terrier that loves a job to do. Friendly, tireless and needs plenty of exercise.

Pekingese.text: Bred for Chinese royalty and still acts the part. Brave and loyal, but keeps strangers at a distance.

Peruvian Hairless Dog (Large).text: A sleek, mostly hairless dog with ancient Peruvian roots. Graceful and lively, and affectionate with its family.

Peruvian Hairless Dog (Medium).text: An elegant, mostly hairless dog from Peru. Loving at home, lively and quick, and wary of people it doesn't know.

Peruvian Hairless Dog (Small).text: A small, sleek hairless dog with ancient Peruvian roots. Affectionate with its people and a keen little watchdog.

Petit Basset Griffon Vendeen.text: A shaggy, merry little French hound. Bold and busy on a scent, and happy to do things its own way.

Pharaoh Hound.text: A sleek, tan hound known to blush when excited. Sharp, alert and quick to spot movement.

Pointer.text: Famous for freezing mid-step to point at game. Dignified and friendly, always scanning the horizon.

Polish Lowland Sheepdog.text: A shaggy, medium-sized herder with a sharp mind and a good memory. Watchful with strangers and very trainable.

Pomeranian.text: A bold, bubbly fluffball with plenty to say. Bright and keen to watch everything going on.

Poodle (Miniature).text: A mid-sized poodle that's bright, active and proud. Learns quickly and enjoys tricks and dog sports.

Poodle (Standard).text: The original poodle, bred to retrieve from water. Very smart and athletic, yet calm and well-mannered at home.

Poodle (Toy).text: A tiny, bright poodle that loves being close to its people. Quick to learn and full of fun.

Porcelaine.text: A sleek French pack hound bred to hunt hare. Gentle at home, but follows its nose its own way.

Portuguese Podengo - Small Medium Large.text: A lively, intelligent hunting dog that comes in three sizes. Keen-eyed and makes a good watchdog.

Portuguese Water Dog.text: A curly-coated fisherman's helper that loves a swim. Full of energy, quick to learn, with a mind of its own.

Prague Ratter.text: One of the smallest breeds around. Lively and alert, but loves curling up with its people after a busy day.

Pug.text: A sociable lap dog that loves people and attention. Snores, snuffles and rarely wants a long run.

Pugalier.text: A Pug-Cavalier cross with a squishy face and a loving nature. Playful in short bursts, then happy to snooze.

Puggle.text: A Beagle-Pug mix with a wrinkly face and a curious nose. Social and fun, with more get-up-and-go than a Pug.

Puli.text: Known for its dreadlock-like cords that bounce as it moves. A tireless worker, lively with family but reserved with strangers.

Pumi.text: A curly-coated Hungarian herder with perky, tipped ears. Busy, bold and full of energy, it loves having a job to do.

Pyrenean Mastiff.text: A huge Spanish guardian with a gentle face. Calm and friendly with family, carrying its size with quiet dignity.

Pyrenean Mountain Dog.text: A big white guardian that's quietly confident. Relaxed most of the time, but serious about protecting its patch.

Pyrenean Sheepdog Longhaired.text: A small, scruffy mountain herder from the Pyrenees. Quick-witted and courageous, and very devoted to its person.

Rhodesian Ridgeback.text: Calm and reserved with strangers, devoted at home. Strong and athletic, with a mind of its own.

Rottweiler.text: A strong, confident guardian that's calm and steady when well raised. Loyal to its family and responds well to training.

Russian Black Terrier.text: Not really a terrier but a big, bearded working dog bred as a guard. Self-assured, lively and friendly with its people.

Russian Toy (Russkiy Toy) (Long Haired).text: Cheerful, busy and curious about everything. Devoted to its owner and wary of strangers.

Russian Toy (Russkiy Toy) (Smooth Haired.text: Tiny, leggy and lively, with a cheerful outlook. Forms a strong bond with its owner.

Saluki.text: Graceful and quiet, often aloof with strangers. A gentle soul with a strong urge to chase.

Samoyed.text: A fluffy white sled dog with a trademark smile. Smart, lively and famously affectionate towards everyone.

Schipperke.text: A small black Belgian barge dog with a fox-like face. Clever, curious and loyal, it loves to keep watch.

Schnauzer.text: A bearded, medium-sized farm dog with bushy eyebrows. Lively, watchful and clever, it makes a keen little guard dog.

Schnauzer (Giant).text: The biggest of the schnauzers, originally a cattle and guard dog. Bold, tireless and needs plenty of work and exercise.

Schnauzer (Miniature).text: Bright and chatty, a keen watchdog. Small, sturdy and happy to join any activity.

Scottish Terrier.text: Short-legged and serious, with a proud, independent air. Brave and deeply loyal to its own people.

Sealyham Terrier.text: A low, white Welsh terrier with a big beard. Bold and watchful, but friendly once it knows you.

Shar Pei.text: Instantly known by its deep wrinkles and hippo-like muzzle. Calm and independent, but affectionate with its own family.

Shetland Sheepdog.text: Looks like a mini Rough Collie. Gentle and loving with family, quick to learn, but often shy with strangers.

Shiba Inu.text: A small, fox-like Japanese hunter with a curled tail. Alert and loyal, but famously independent and cat-like.

Shih Tzu.text: A little lion dog with a flowing coat. Friendly and outgoing with a cheeky independent streak, made for companionship.

Shikoku.text: A rare Japanese hunting dog with a wolfish look. Energetic and alert, with plenty of stamina for long outings.

Siberian Husky.text: A sled dog with striking eyes and a love of running. Friendly to all, but needs lots of exercise and loves to talk.

Skye Terrier.text: Elegant and steady, usually devoted to one special person. Cautious around people it doesn't know.

Sloughi.text: A graceful North African sighthound. Proud and reserved, but deeply devoted to its family.

Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.text: Bouncy and affectionate, famous for its exuberant greetings. Loves people and has energy to burn.

Spanish Mastiff.text: A giant, easygoing Spanish livestock guardian. Calm and affectionate with family, and protective of its home.

Spanish Water Dog.text: A woolly herding and water dog from Spain. Loyal and quick to learn, it loves a job to do.

St Bernard.text: The famous Alpine rescue dog. A big, friendly softie that's calm indoors and still enjoys a good romp outside.

Staffordshire Bull Terrier.text: Muscular but soft-hearted, famously devoted to its family. Full of energy and keen on a game.

Sussex Spaniel.text: A kindly, steady spaniel that's often vocal when working. Easygoing and relaxed at home.

Swedish Lapphund.text: A fluffy, usually black spitz once used to herd reindeer. Hard-working, keen to learn and full of stamina.

Swedish Vallhund.text: A short-legged Viking cattle dog with a wolfish coat. Cheerful and friendly, always watching what's going on.

Tatra Shepherd Dog.text: A big white Polish mountain guardian. Calm and sensible by nature, but always alert to anything unusual on its patch.

Tenterfield Terrier.text: A small Aussie terrier, watchful and plucky. Fiercely loyal to its family and fearless for its size.

Tibetan Mastiff.text: A massive, heavily maned guardian from the Himalayas. Calm and aloof with strangers, and very protective of its home.

Tibetan Spaniel.text: Bright and self-assured, often keeping watch from a high perch. Aloof with strangers but loving with family.

Tibetan Terrier.text: Not a true terrier but a shaggy Himalayan companion. Friendly and clever, and watchful of newcomers.

Tornjak.text: A large mountain guardian from the Balkans. Calm and devoted with family, and protective of its flock and home.

Weimaraner.text: The sleek silver-grey ghost of the dog park. Bursting with energy, loves to work and sticks close to its people.

Weimaraner (Longhair).text: A rarer, feathery-coated version of the silver hunting dog. Energetic, loving and happiest with a job to do.

Welsh Corgi (Cardigan).text: The corgi with the long, bushy tail. A steady, clever cattle herder that keeps a watchful eye on everything.

Welsh Corgi (Pembroke).text: A short-legged herder with a big personality. Outgoing and bold, and quick to sound off when something's up.

Welsh Springer Spaniel.text: A merry, active spaniel with a kind nature. Tends to stick close to its own family.

Welsh Terrier.text: Cheerful and spirited, with a classic black and tan coat. Brave outdoors and loving at home.

West Highland White Terrier.text: A bright little terrier with a big personality. Independent, but happy to be in the thick of things.

Whippet.text: A gentle, loving couch potato at home. Flies like the wind when it gets the chance to run.

White Swiss Shepherd Dog.text: A white shepherd with a softer nature than many of its cousins. Active and alert outdoors, gentle and calm at home.

Wirehaired Slovakian Pointer.text: A versatile working gundog for field, forest and water. Obedient, easy to train and attached to its handler.

Xoloitzcuintle.text: The ancient hairless dog of Mexico, in three sizes. Calm and friendly at home, and alert to anything new.

Yakutian Laika.text: A striking Siberian sled and hunting dog. Lively and friendly with people, with a bold, hardy spirit.

Yorkshire Terrier.text: Big terrier attitude packed into a silky little body. Bright, busy and quick to sound the alarm.

Yugoslavian Shepherd Dog - Sharplanina.text: A hefty Balkan flock guardian with an even temper. Fiercely devoted to its owner and watchful of strangers.
